Higher AK1 activity preserves erythrocyte ATP, prevents premature haemolysis, and keeps plasma LDH low.

Higher ATIC activity increases de novo IMP production, supporting the cellular ATP pool.

causal:influence:cystinosin_transport_ac.mechanism: Cystinosin deficiency causes lysosomal cystine accumulation in all cells including leukocytes. Leukocyte cystine measurement is the standard diagnostic and monitoring assay for cystinosis; CTNS LoF → leukocyte cystine UP.

causal:influence:cytosolic_calcium_trans.evidence: Bers (2001) Excitation-Contraction Coupling: SERCA2a uptake is steeply Ca2+ dependent and removes the bulk of cytosolic Ca2+ during relaxation; BioModels MODEL7914464799 (Shannon2004, PubMed 15347581). | textbook corroboration: Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-11.5.3 (Membrane ATPases): elevated cytoplasmic Ca2+ activates SERCA-mediated Ca2+ pumping back into the SR after muscle excitation.; Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-12.9 (Cell Motility - Undeclared): 'as cytoplasmic Ca2+ levels rise, the phospholamban releases from the Ca2+ pump and allows it to function.'; Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-4.4 (The Action Potential in Neurons): 'The increased [Ca2+]cytoplasm is taken up by the sarcoplasmic reticulum' and Ca2+-calmodulin relieves inhibition of the Ca2+ pump, increasing Ca2+ removal when [Ca2+] rises. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:cytosolic_calcium_trans.mechanism: elevated cytosolic Ca2+ raises the SERCA2a turnover (quality: cytosolic [Ca2+] -> disposition: SERCA2a Ca2+ affinity on the cytosolic face -> process: ATP-driven Ca2+ pumping into the SR -> quality: SR Ca2+ uptake rate)

causal:influence:dbh_activity:positive:u.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine — dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency (OMIM 223360): absent plasma and urinary norepinephrine and epinephrine; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (dopamine --DBH--> norepinephrine); Williams Textbook of Endocrinology (urinary norepinephrine as catecholamine secretion assay) | intervention: DBH deficiency (DBH gene LoF, OMIM 223360): do(dbh_activity=low) -> urinary_norepinephrine falls to zero
causal:influence:dbh_activity:positive:u.mechanism: dopamine beta-hydroxylase hydroxylates dopamine to norepinephrine in sympathetic nerve terminals and adrenal chromaffin cells; higher DBH activity raises norepinephrine synthesis and urinary excretion; DBH deficiency abolishes norepinephrine and epinephrine synthesis, leaving urinary norepinephrine undetectable

causal:influence:dhcr7_activity:negative.evidence: Wassif CA et al. Nat Genet. 1998;18:107-110; Waterham HR et al. (DHCR7 mutations in SLOS); OMIM 270400 (Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, cholesterol biosynthesis (Kandutsch-Russell pathway) | intervention: DHCR7 loss-of-function (Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome, OMIM 270400): do(DHCR7 activity down) -> plasma 7-DHC up
causal:influence:dhcr7_activity:negative.mechanism: DHCR7 (7-dehydrocholesterol reductase) reduces the C7=C8 double bond of 7-DHC to form cholesterol; loss of DHCR7 causes Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome (SLOS, OMIM 270400) in which 7-DHC accumulates markedly in plasma and tissues.

causal:influence:dhtkd1_activity:negativ.evidence: Alpha-aminoadipic and alpha-ketoadipic aciduria (AAKAD, OMIM 204750); PMID 25860818 (J Inherit Metab Dis 2015) — 'mutations in DHTKD1 … elevated 2-aminoadipate in plasma'; PMC5059180 — 'New Cases of DHTKD1 Mutations in Patients with 2-Ketoadipic Aciduria'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (lysine catabolism: 2-aminoadipate → 2-oxoadipate → glutaryl-CoA step). | intervention: do(DHTKD1 activity ↓) = alpha-aminoadipic and alpha-ketoadipic aciduria (OMIM 204750) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:dhtkd1_activity:negativ.mechanism: DHTKD1 encodes the E1 subunit of the 2-oxoadipate dehydrogenase complex, which oxidatively decarboxylates 2-oxoadipate to glutaryl-CoA in the final common step of lysine, tryptophan, and hydroxylysine catabolism. With DHTKD1 deficiency, 2-oxoadipate accumulates and equilibrates with 2-aminoadipate by transamination, raising plasma 2-aminoadipate (∂[2-AA]/∂(DHTKD1 activity) < 0).

causal:influence:duodenal_chyme_acidity:.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.66 (Physiology of Gastrointestinal Disorders) §Peptic Ulcer / Basic Cause of Peptic Ulceration: “it reflexly inhibits gastric secretion and peristalsis in the stomach, both by nervous reflexes and by hormonal feedback from the duodenum, thereby decreasing the rate of gastric emptying”
causal:influence:duodenal_chyme_acidity:.mechanism: duodenal acid activates the enterogastric reflex that inhibits gastric peristalsis, slowing delivery of chyme from stomach to duodenum

causal:influence:duodenal_trypsin_activi.evidence: Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-6.6.3 (Zymogen Activation): 'Once activated, trypsin will cleave and activate other zymogen proteases and lipases in the duodenum. causal:influence:duodenal_trypsin_activi.mechanism: Trypsin proteolytically cleaves and activates prolipase to lipase in the duodenal lumen.

causal:influence:eaat3_activity:negative.evidence: Dicarboxylic aminoaciduria OMIM 222730; PMC3007158 / JCI 2011 (PMID 21123949): 'Loss-of-function mutations in the glutamate transporter SLC1A1 cause human dicarboxylic aminoaciduria'; Bailey et al. identified SLC1A1 R445W and other LoF mutations causing elevated urinary glutamate; Boron & Boulpaep (renal glutamate handling). | intervention: do(SLC1A1 loss-of-function) — dicarboxylic aminoaciduria OMIM 222730 [citations PubMed-verified]

LoF mutations in SLC1A1 cause dicarboxylic aminoaciduria: failure to reabsorb glutamate (and aspartate) from glomerular filtrate leads to elevated urinary glutamate. do(SLC1A1 LoF) -> urinary glutamate rises.

causal:influence:end_diastolic_volume:po.evidence: Levin et al. 1998, NEJM (NT-proBNP co-secreted with BNP from ventricular myocytes under wall stress). Maisel et al. 2002, NEJM (NT-proBNP for diagnosis of heart failure: elevated in proportion to ventricular volume overload/wall stress). Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (natriuretic peptide processing). | intervention: Volume loading / congestive heart failure (elevated EDV): NT-proBNP rises in parallel with BNP; its longer half-life makes it a robust clinical biomarker of ventricular stretch
causal:influence:end_diastolic_volume:po.mechanism: NT-proBNP is the biologically inert N-terminal fragment cleaved from proBNP upon secretion from ventricular cardiomyocytes; proBNP secretion is triggered by the same myocardial wall stretch that drives BNP; NT-proBNP and BNP are produced in a 1:1 molar ratio from the same cleavage event

causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:li.evidence: Lehninger 7th ed. ch.17 & ch.23 (epinephrine mobilizes fatty acids); Boron & Boulpaep 3rd ed. ch.51
causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:li.mechanism: beta-adrenergic activation of hormone-sensitive lipase in adipocytes

causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:me.evidence: "the epinephrine secreted by the adrenal medullae can increase the metabolic rate of the whole body often to as much as 100 per cent above normal" — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 60, p. 754-755
causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:me.mechanism: adrenal epinephrine calorigenic effect: raises whole-body metabolic rate (up to ~100% above normal) and basal metabolic rate

causal:influence:erythrocyte_23_bpg:nega.evidence: Jakubowski & Flatt Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-5.03.4: '2,3-bisphosphoglycerate … shift the binding curves of Hb for oxygen to the right, lowering the apparent affinity of Hb for oxygen.' BPGM deficiency (OMIM 222800): very low erythrocyte 2,3-BPG → left-shifted ODC → high SaO₂ at physiological PO₂ — genetic evidence for the negative sign. | intervention: Mechanistic model: BPGM LoF (OMIM 222800) demonstrates that low 2,3-BPG → high Hb-O₂ saturation (negative slope confirmed). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:erythrocyte_23_bpg:nega.mechanism: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate binds preferentially to deoxyhaemoglobin (T-state) in a pocket between the β-chains, stabilising the low-affinity T-state and shifting the O₂–Hb dissociation curve rightward (lower P₅₀). Higher erythrocyte [2,3-BPG] therefore decreases Hb-O₂ affinity and reduces Hb-O₂ saturation at any given PO₂.

causal:influence:erythrocyte_itp:negativ.evidence: ITPase deficiency causes a Martsolf-like syndrome with lethal infantile dilated cardiomyopathy (Mayr et al., PLOS Genetics 2019, PMID:30856165; PMC:PMC6428344). Cardiac involvement in 28.6% of patients with ITPA deficiency; rI misincorporation in RNA correlates with organ dysfunction severity, highest in embryonic heart. | intervention: do(ITPA loss-of-function): complete ITPase deficiency → ITP accumulates → rI misincorporated into cardiac RNA → cardiomyocyte dysfunction → reduced contractility [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:erythrocyte_itp:negativ.mechanism: ITPA deficiency → erythrocyte (and tissue) ITP accumulation → inosine (rI) misincorporation into cardiac RNA → proteotoxic RNA dysfunction and mitochondrial damage → dilated cardiomyopathy → reduced myocardial contractility; highest rI accumulation seen in embryonic heart (Martsolf-like syndrome, PMID:30856165)

causal:influence:erythropoietin:positive.evidence: "The principal stimulus for red blood cell production in low oxygen states is a circulating hormone called erythropoietin ... In the absence of erythropoietin, hypoxia has little or no effect in stimulating red blood cell production." — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 32, p. 422-423
causal:influence:erythropoietin:positive.mechanism: EPO binds and dimerizes the erythropoietin receptor (EPOR) on erythroid progenitors -> receptor activation

causal:influence:fgf23:negative:renal_ph.evidence: Shimada et al., J Clin Invest 2004, PMID 14966565, DOI 10.1172/JCI19081: targeted Fgf23 ablation caused increased renal phosphate reabsorption and hyperphosphatemia; Shimada et al., J Bone Miner Res 2004, PMID 15040831, DOI 10.1359/JBMR.0301264: recombinant FGF23 administration reduced renal NaPi-2a and serum phosphate.
causal:influence:fgf23:negative:renal_ph.mechanism: FGF23 (via renal alpha-klotho) downregulates proximal-tubule NaPi-IIa/IIc cotransporters -> phosphaturia

causal:influence:folr1_activity:positive.evidence: Cerebral folate deficiency (FOLR1 deficiency/antibodies, OMIM 613068): Ramaekers et al. (2004) Brain 127:1360-1380 (FOLR1 deficiency causes low CSF 5-MTHF, low CSF 5-HIAA and HVA); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (cerebral folate deficiency: low CSF 5-MTHF associated with low BH4, 5-HIAA, HVA). Intervention: do(FOLR1 LoF). | intervention: genetic loss-of-function or autoantibody blockade of FOLR1 (cerebral folate deficiency, OMIM 613068)
causal:influence:folr1_activity:positive.mechanism: Folate receptor alpha (FOLR1) mediates the transport of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF) across the choroid plexus into cerebrospinal fluid. FOLR1 deficiency or blocking autoantibodies (cerebral folate deficiency, OMIM 613068) causes markedly low CSF 5-MTHF, which impairs folate-dependent regeneration of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) and disrupts the methylation cycle. BH4 is the obligatory cofactor for tryptophan hydroxylase (serotonin biosynthesis); reduced BH4 lowers serotonin production and CSF 5-HIAA. Active FOLR1 maintains adequate CSF 5-MTHF -> BH4 -> serotonin -> 5-HIAA.

causal:influence:free_t3:positive:sa_nod.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep; clinical hyperthyroid tachycardia / hypothyroid bradycardia | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-092 (17.5: The Thyroid Gland): 'When levels of T3 and T4 hormones are excessive, this effect accelerates the heart rate' | re-routed free_t3->heart_rate through sa_node_automaticity per G. causal:influence:free_t3:positive:sa_nod.mechanism: T3 positive chronotropy via SA-node automaticity (raises If/funny current, L-type Ca current, SERCA Ca cycling, Na/K-ATPase -> steeper phase-4 depolarisation); see george_heart_rate.yaml

causal:influence:free_t4:negative:pituit.evidence: "the rate of TSH secretion is exquisitely sensitive to the plasma concentrations of free thyroid hormones" and "Because the concentration of TSH is inversely proportional to the degree of thyroid hormone excess, patients with clinical symptoms almost invariably have serum TSH concentrations below 0.1 mU/L." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 11, p. 356/358
causal:influence:free_t4:negative:pituit.mechanism: free T4 (and T3) exert negative feedback on thyrotrophs; TSH concentration is inversely proportional to free thyroid hormone supply

causal:influence:galactokinase_activity:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 15 (Leloir pathway first step: galactokinase phosphorylates galactose); Scriver's OMMBID (GALK deficiency / galactosemia type II, OMIM 230200: hypergalactosaemia, cataracts from galactitol in lens); Harrison's (galactose metabolism disorders). | intervention: GALK1 loss-of-function (galactosemia type II, OMIM 230200): do(galactokinase_activity↓) → plasma galactose accumulates
causal:influence:galactokinase_activity:.mechanism: GALK1 (galactokinase) catalyzes the first step of the Leloir pathway: galactose + ATP → galactose-1-phosphate + ADP. GALK1 LoF (galactosemia type II / GALK deficiency, OMIM 230200) → galactose is not phosphorylated → plasma galactose accumulates. GALK activity ↑ → galactose rapidly phosphorylated → plasma galactose ↓.

causal:influence:gamt_activity:negative:.evidence: Lehninger, creatine biosynthesis; OMMBID GAMT deficiency — ELEVATED guanidinoacetate (plasma/urine/CSF)
causal:influence:gamt_activity:negative:.mechanism: GAMT methylates guanidinoacetate -> creatine; reduced GAMT activity causes guanidinoacetate to accumulate

causal:influence:gamt_activity:positive:.evidence: GAMT deficiency / cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome 2 OMIM 612736; PubMed 9322805 (Schulze et al. 1997, 'Guanidino compounds in GAMT deficiency' — creatine concentrations low in plasma, CSF and urine); NORD GAMT deficiency (creatine supplementation restores plasma creatine); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (creatine biosynthesis: AGAT then GAMT). | intervention: do(gamt_activity ↓) — GAMT deficiency (autosomal recessive) OMIM 612736 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:gamt_activity:positive:.mechanism: Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) methylates guanidinoacetate to produce creatine (second and final step of creatine biosynthesis, occurring mainly in liver). LoF of GAMT abolishes this production, causing creatine depletion in plasma and tissues (∂[creatine]/∂GAMT_activity > 0).

causal:influence:gi_parasympathetic_tone.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-080 (15.2: Divisions of the Autonomic Nervous System): parasympathetic activity increases GI motility; muscarinic agonists (bethanechol) increase intestinal motility in clinical use. Atropine (muscarinic antagonist, do(gi_parasympathetic_tone -)) reduces GI motility. | intervention: Bethanechol (muscarinic agonist) / do(gi_parasympathetic_tone +): increases GI motility; atropine / do(gi_parasympathetic_tone -): decreases GI motility
causal:influence:gi_parasympathetic_tone.mechanism: Vagal efferents release acetylcholine onto enteric neurons and smooth muscle cells in the GI wall; ACh binding to M2/M3 muscarinic receptors on smooth muscle cells promotes contraction and propagation of peristaltic waves, increasing overall GI motility.

causal:influence:gi_sympathetic_tone:neg.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-080 (15.2: Divisions of the Autonomic Nervous System): sympathetic activation causes 'The digestive system shuts down so that blood is not absorbing nutrients when it should be delivering oxygen to skeletal muscles' — directly describing GI motility inhibition. | intervention: Epinephrine infusion / do(gi_sympathetic_tone +): reduces GI motility (ileus induction); alpha-adrenergic blockade reduces this inhibition (clinical perioperative management)
causal:influence:gi_sympathetic_tone:neg.mechanism: Sympathetic nerve fibers release norepinephrine onto enteric neurons (presynaptically) and GI smooth muscle; this inhibits enteric neuron activity and smooth-muscle contraction, reducing peristaltic force and frequency. The physiological role is to arrest digestion during fight-or-flight.

causal:influence:gla_activity:positive:g.evidence: Fabry disease OMIM 301500 (GLA LoF); Schiffmann et al., NEJM 2001 (enzyme replacement in Fabry: renal function protection); Germain, Orphanet J Rare Dis 2010 (Fabry nephropathy: Gb3 accumulation in all renal cell types; GFR decline in males from 3rd-4th decade). Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Lysosomal Storage Diseases (Fabry disease: renal involvement causes progressive renal failure). | intervention: GLA loss-of-function (Fabry disease, OMIM 301500)
causal:influence:gla_activity:positive:g.mechanism: Alpha-galactosidase A (GLA) deficiency (Fabry disease, OMIM 301500) causes globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) to accumulate in renal tubular cells, glomerular endothelial cells, mesangial cells, and podocytes. Progressive Gb3 storage leads to podocyte vacuolation, glomerulosclerosis, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis — the hallmark Fabry nephropathy — causing progressive reduction in GFR and end-stage renal disease in untreated males. do(GLA LoF) → Gb3 storage in kidney → nephropathy → GFR falls.

causal:influence:glutamate_dehydrogenase.evidence: Hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome (HI/HA), OMIM:606762 — GLUD1 GoF causes hyperammonemia; plasma ammonia chronically elevated (100-200 μmol/L) due to over-active glutamate dehydrogenase; the same edge direction applies: more GLUD1 activity -> more ammonia
causal:influence:glutamate_dehydrogenase.mechanism: RHEA:11612 (EC 1.4.1.3): L-glutamate + NADP(+) + H2O = 2-oxoglutarate + NH4(+) + NADPH + H(+); NH4+ (ammonia) is the direct product; GLUD1 gain-of-function (activating mutation) increases enzyme flux and NH4+ production; edge sign reflects enzyme_activity -> product relationship (applicable for both GoF assessment and the underlying physiology)

causal:influence:gnrh:positive:pituitary.evidence: "Pulsatile GnRH administration normalizes pulsatile LH but not testosterone secretion, consistent with an impairment of hypothalamic GnRH secretion occurring in combination with a primary defect in testosterone production by the testis" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p. 724
causal:influence:gnrh:positive:pituitary.mechanism: pulsatile GnRH stimulates pituitary gonadotroph LH secretion; exogenous pulsatile GnRH administration normalizes pulsatile LH

causal:influence:gr_activity:positive:g6.evidence: INTERVENTIONAL (pharmacological + perturbation). Dexamethasone induces hepatic G6Pase and raises glucose output; mifepristone and liver GR knockout blunt the induction. DRAFT for domain review (primary citations pending verification).

causal:influence:hemoglobin_o2_saturatio.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.40 (Transport of Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide in Blood and Tissue Fluids) §When Oxygen Binds with Hemoglobin, Carbon Dioxide Is Released (the Haldane Effect): “binding of oxygen with hemoglobin tends to displace carbon dioxide from the blood. Indeed, this effect, called the Haldane effect”
causal:influence:hemoglobin_o2_saturatio.mechanism: O2 binding makes hemoglobin a stronger acid (oxygenation -> conformational acidity -> displacement) that releases bound CO2 and H+, lowering blood CO2 content/PCO2

causal:influence:hepatic_conjugated_bili.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (canalicular MRP2/ABCC2 export of conjugated bilirubin); Harrison's, 'Jaundice' — Dubin-Johnson syndrome (ABCC2/MRP2 LoF; OMIM 237500) causes conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
causal:influence:hepatic_conjugated_bili.mechanism: MRP2/ABCC2 actively transports conjugated bilirubin across the canalicular membrane into bile; higher excretion clears the hepatocyte conjugated pool and lowers plasma conjugated bilirubin (MRP2 LoF therefore RAISES plasma conjugated bilirubin)

causal:influence:hepatic_glycogen_syntha.evidence: Hepatic glycogen synthase deficiency (GSD type 0a), OMIM:240600 — LoF causes fasting hypoglycemia (low plasma glucose after overnight fast) due to absent hepatic glycogen stores
causal:influence:hepatic_glycogen_syntha.mechanism: RHEA:18549 (EC 2.4.1.11): postprandial glucose is stored as hepatic glycogen via GYS2; failure to store glycogen means fasting glucose supply from glycogenolysis is absent, leading to fasting hypoglycemia

causal:influence:hepatic_urea_synthesis:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (ureagenesis as ammonia detoxification); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (hepatic ammonia clearance); OTC deficiency OMIM 311250 | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-141 (24.5: Protein Metabolism): 'In the urea cycle, ammonium is combined with CO2, resulting in urea and water. The urea is eliminated through the kidneys in the urine' — urea synthesis removes ammonia from circulation
causal:influence:hepatic_urea_synthesis:.mechanism: urea synthesis is the principal route of ammonia disposal; higher hepatic ureagenesis lowers the circulating ammonia load, so reduced urea synthesis raises plasma ammonia (hyperammonemia of urea-cycle disorders).

causal:influence:hepatocyte_cholesterol_.evidence: Brown & Goldstein Science 1986 (sterol feedback downregulates LDLR via SREBP); BioModels BIOMD0000000434 (McAuley2012)
causal:influence:hepatocyte_cholesterol_.mechanism: high intracellular cholesterol -> SREBP cleavage suppressed -> reduced LDLR transcription -> lower LDLR surface activity

causal:influence:hoga1_activity:negative.evidence: Belostotsky et al., 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase inactivity in PH3 and glyoxylate reductase inhibition (PMID 22771891); Monico/Milliner, PH3 is caused by mutations in HOGA1 (PMID 22391140); OMIM 613616 (PH3): elevated urinary 4-OH-2-oxoglutarate is the biochemical hallmark | intervention: Primary hyperoxaluria type 3 (HOGA1 loss-of-function, OMIM 613616) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:hoga1_activity:negative.mechanism: HOGA1 (4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate aldolase) cleaves 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate (HOG) to pyruvate and glyoxylate in the 4-hydroxyproline catabolism pathway; HOGA1 deficiency (primary hyperoxaluria type 3) leaves HOG unconsumed, raising urinary 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate — reduced HOGA1 activity raises urinary 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate

causal:influence:hydroxyacyl_coa_dehydro.evidence: 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (HADH, OMIM 231530): Kapoor et al. J Clin Invest 2009; PMC3509842 ('plasma 3-hydroxybutyrylcarnitine... invariably present'); MedlinePlus Genetics 'familial hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia caused by SCHAD deficiency' | intervention: loss-of-function of HADH gene (3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, OMIM 231530) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:hydroxyacyl_coa_dehydro.mechanism: Mitochondrial 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (HADH, the medium/short-chain enzyme encoded by the HADH gene) oxidizes 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA (C4-OH-CoA) to acetoacetyl-CoA; reduced HADH activity causes 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA to accumulate and be esterified to carnitine, raising plasma 3-hydroxybutyrylcarnitine (C4-OH), the principal diagnostic biomarker of HADH deficiency

causal:influence:hypothalamic_glutamater.evidence: Excitatory NMDA stimulates LH release in neonatal and adult rats, fetal sheep, and prepubertal and adult rhesus monkeys... NMDA evokes an LH pulse mediated by GnRH. Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 26
causal:influence:hypothalamic_glutamater.mechanism: NMDA (excitatory glutamate receptor agonist) stimulates LH release via GnRH pulse generator activation

causal:influence:iduronate_sulfatase_act.evidence: Brady et al. Metabolic Bases of Inherited Disease: MPS II involves storage of both HS and DS; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 7 (GAG structure and catabolism) | intervention: do(IDS activity down) = Hunter syndrome / MPS II (OMIM 309900): urinary dermatan sulfate elevated along with heparan sulfate [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:iduronate_sulfatase_act.mechanism: IDS cleaves 2-O-sulfate from iduronate in dermatan sulfate (a GAG chain rich in iduronate-2-sulfate). When IDS is deficient (Hunter syndrome / MPS II), both heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate accumulate and are excreted in urine.

causal:influence:il6:positive:plasma_pla.evidence: Mechanism: IL-6 -> STAT3/C/EBPbeta -> increased hepatic PLG transcription -> higher plasma plasminogen (modest positive acute-phase reactant). Intervention: do(selenium deficiency) -> low DIO1/DIO2 selenoprotein activity -> impaired T4->T3 conversion -> low free T3.

causal:influence:presynaptic_neurotransm.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-35.2 (35.2 How Neurons Communicate): 'The signal arrives at the synapse and causes neurotransmitter molecules to be released from vesicles into the synaptic cleft.' Tetanus toxin (proteolytic cleavage of VAMP/synaptobrevin) blocks vesicle fusion → abolishes neurotransmitter release and synaptic ACh elevation; botulinum toxin similarly, confirming presynaptic release rate drives synaptic [ACh]. | intervention: Pharmacological: Ca²⁺ ionophore (ionomycin) or presynaptic voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channel agonists increase vesicle exocytosis and raise synaptic [ACh]; botulinum toxin/tetanus toxin LoF blocks exocytosis and abolishes the synaptic concentration rise.
causal:influence:presynaptic_neurotransm.mechanism: Presynaptic vesicle exocytosis (Ca²⁺-triggered SNARE complex fusion) releases neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft; greater vesicle exocytosis rate directly raises synaptic ACh concentration (and other neurotransmitters). Applies equivalently to cholinergic, GABAergic and aminergic synapses; modeled here for acetylcholine as the archetypical example.

causal:influence:prss1_acinar_activity:p.evidence: Hereditary pancreatitis (OMIM 167800): PRSS1 R122H and N29I GoF mutations cause elevated plasma trypsinogen and pancreatitis (PRSS1-Related Hereditary Pancreatitis, GeneReviews NBK84399; Human cationic trypsinogen PRSS1 variants and chronic pancreatitis PMC3949028; Trypsin activity governs increased susceptibility to pancreatitis in mice expressing PRSS1-R122H PMC6934224); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (pancreatic zymogen secretion and activation) | intervention: do(PRSS1 GoF) — PRSS1 R122H or N29I gain-of-function variant → hereditary pancreatitis → elevated plasma trypsinogen; also triplication of PRSS1 locus (gene-dosage GoF, Nature Genetics 2006)
causal:influence:prss1_acinar_activity:p.mechanism: Gain-of-function mutations in PRSS1 (encoding cationic trypsinogen, the predominant ~60% of pancreatic trypsinogen) accelerate trypsinogen autoactivation and/or inhibit chymotrypsin C-dependent degradation; intrapancreatic trypsin activation triggers pancreatitis with release of trypsinogen/trypsin into the bloodstream, elevating plasma trypsinogen concentration

causal:influence:pulmonary_lymph_flow:ne.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.38 (Pulmonary Circulation, Pulmonary Edema, Pleural Fluid) §Fluid in the Pleural Cavity: “the excess fluid is pumped away by lymphatic vessels opening directly from the pleural cavity”

causal:influence:pyruvate_carboxylase_ac.evidence: Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency (OMIM 266150): GeneReviews NBK6852 — 'elevated levels of plasma lysine, citrulline, alanine, and proline'; Cureus PMC8202815 — 'elevated plasma alanine ... likely secondary to the increased level of pyruvate'; Merck Manual 'Pyruvate Metabolism Disorders' — hyperalaninemia is a consistent laboratory finding in PC deficiency; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 16 (pyruvate carboxylase and pyruvate disposal). | intervention: do(PC activity ↓) = pyruvate carboxylase deficiency (OMIM 266150)
causal:influence:pyruvate_carboxylase_ac.mechanism: Pyruvate carboxylase (PC) converts pyruvate to oxaloacetate, entering the TCA cycle. In PC deficiency, pyruvate accumulates and is redirected by alanine aminotransferase (ALT) to alanine; thus higher PC activity clears pyruvate and lowers alanine (∂[Ala]/∂(PC activity) < 0). LoF of PC → pyruvate up → alanine up (hyperalaninemia secondary to hyperpyruvataemia).

causal:influence:qdpr_activity:negative:.evidence: Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (DHPR/QDPR deficiency: elevated urinary biopterin, normal/near-normal neopterin — OMIM #261630); PreventionGenetics DHPR deficiency test note: 'biopterin is highly elevated' in DHPR deficiency. | intervention: loss-of-function of QDPR (DHPR deficiency)
causal:influence:qdpr_activity:negative:.mechanism: Dihydropteridine reductase (QDPR) regenerates BH4 from quinonoid-BH2; QDPR deficiency (DHPR deficiency, OMIM #261630) blocks regeneration causing BH2/biopterin to accumulate. Biopterin (the oxidised pterin) spills into urine and is markedly elevated — the hallmark biochemical marker of DHPR deficiency.

causal:influence:qdpr_activity:positive:.evidence: DHPR/QDPR deficiency OMIM 261630; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (DHPR deficiency: 'CSF tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) is markedly reduced'; 'failure to regenerate BH4 causes severe neurotransmitter deficiency'). PMC11743392 (UAE BH4 disorder cohort: CSF BH4 severely reduced in DHPR deficiency). Kaufman, Proc Natl Acad Sci 1975 (DHPR regenerates BH4 in the hydroxylase catalytic cycle). | intervention: QDPR (DHPR) loss-of-function (DHPR deficiency, OMIM 261630) | intervention: QDPR/DHPR loss-of-function (OMIM 261630)
causal:influence:qdpr_activity:positive:.mechanism: Dihydropteridine reductase (QDPR) regenerates tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) from quinonoid-dihydrobiopterin (qBH2) in the aromatic amino acid hydroxylase reactions (phenylalanine hydroxylase, tyrosine hydroxylase, tryptophan hydroxylase). QDPR deficiency (DHPR deficiency; OMIM 261630) abolishes BH4 regeneration; BH4 is consumed and not recycled, causing CSF BH4 to fall while biopterin (the fully oxidized form) accumulates. Low CSF BH4 impairs neurotransmitter synthesis (dopamine, norepinephrine, serotonin) causing severe progressive neurological disease. do(QDPR LoF) → BH4 not regenerated → CSF BH4 falls.

causal:influence:right_atrial_pressure:p.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.9 (Heart Muscle; The Heart as a Pump and Function of the Heart Valves) §What Is the Explanation of the Frank-Starling Mechanism?: “Stretch of the right atrial wall directly increases the heart rate by 10 to 20 per cent; this, too, helps increase the amount of blood pumped each minute”
causal:influence:right_atrial_pressure:p.mechanism: stretch of the right atrial wall (raised right atrial pressure/filling) directly increases pacemaker firing, raising heart rate (Bainbridge effect)

causal:influence:sarcolemmal_permeabilit.evidence: Serum myoglobin in muscular dystrophy PubMed 7374673 (elevated serum myoglobin in 91.7% of DMD patients); ScienceDirect myoglobinuria in DMD (myoglobin released from fragile sarcolemma); OMIM 310200; Harrison's 'Rhabdomyolysis' (myoglobin as early plasma marker of muscle necrosis). | intervention: do(sarcolemmal_permeability ↑) — Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD LoF) / rhabdomyolysis [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:sarcolemmal_permeabilit.mechanism: Myoglobin is a small (17 kDa) heme-containing oxygen-storage protein of skeletal muscle fibres; its small size means it leaks rapidly into plasma when the sarcolemma is damaged, and then is filtered by the kidney. Elevated serum myoglobin is a sensitive early marker of rhabdomyolysis.

causal:influence:scd_activity:positive:p.evidence: Miyazaki et al., J Biol Chem 2001 (SCD1 knockout mice: reduced monounsaturated fatty acids); Ntambi et al., PNAS 2002 (SCD1 deficiency phenotype); Lehninger, Ch. 21 (delta-9 desaturation of myristate to myristoleate by SCD). | intervention: SCD loss-of-function: SCD LoF -> failure of delta-9 desaturation of myristate -> reduced plasma myristoleate [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:scd_activity:positive:p.mechanism: Stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD/SCD1) inserts a cis-double bond at the delta-9 position of saturated fatty acyl-CoAs. It acts on myristoyl-CoA (C14:0) to produce myristoleoyl-CoA (C14:1n-5), and on palmitoyl-CoA (C16:0) to produce palmitoleoyl-CoA (C16:1n-7) and on stearoyl-CoA to produce oleoyl-CoA (C18:1n-9). SCD deficiency reduces plasma monounsaturated fatty acids including myristoleate.

causal:influence:scot_activity:negative:.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray 'Inborn Metabolic Diseases': SCOT (OXCT1) deficiency (OMIM 245050) — hallmark is persistent, non-fasting ketoacidosis because acetoacetate cannot be activated for peripheral oxidation; plasma 3-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate markedly elevated. Mechanism: Lehninger Ch.17 (ketone-body utilisation, SCOT role). | intervention: SCOT deficiency (OXCT1 LoF, OMIM 245050): peripheral ketolysis abolished → plasma acetoacetate and 3-hydroxybutyrate rise persistently
causal:influence:scot_activity:negative:.mechanism: SCOT (succinyl-CoA:3-oxoacid-CoA transferase, OXCT1) catalyses the rate-limiting step of peripheral ketone-body oxidation: activating acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA for further catabolism. SCOT is absent from liver, so its activity determines extrahepatic ketone utilisation. do(SCOT_activity UP) → more acetoacetate activated and oxidised → plasma ketone bodies fall. SCOT deficiency (OMIM 245050) causes permanent non-fasting ketoacidosis because ketone bodies cannot be consumed peripherally.

causal:influence:sepiapterin_reductase_a.evidence: Sepiapterin reductase deficiency OMIM 612716; PMC10996339 (SPR deficiency: low BH4, low HVA and 5-HIAA in CSF; dopa-responsive dystonia due to BH4 deficiency); hpo_csf_markers fragment edge csf_dihydrobiopterin -> csf_tetrahydrobiopterin encodes the next step; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (tetrahydrobiopterin biosynthesis and regeneration). | intervention: SPR biallelic loss-of-function (OMIM 612716): CSF BH4 (tetrahydrobiopterin) falls to very low levels
causal:influence:sepiapterin_reductase_a.mechanism: SPR is required for the final reduction steps in de novo BH4 biosynthesis (sepiapterin -> BH2 -> BH4 via SPR and DHPR/DHFR). SPR loss-of-function causes severe CSF BH4 deficiency because the de novo route is blocked at this step, even though neopterin pathway flux upstream is normal. More SPR activity supports higher CSF BH4 production.

causal:influence:slc6a6_activity:positiv.evidence: ScienceDirect 2008 (TauT/Slc6a6 KO mouse): 'taurine depletion caused by knocking out the taurine transporter gene leads to cardiomyopathy with cardiac atrophy'; OMIM 186854 (SLC6A6); Spandidos MMR 2020 (taurine transporter homeostasis review). | intervention: do(SLC6A6 loss-of-function) — hypotaurinemic retinal degeneration and cardiomyopathy: SLC6A6 activity DOWN -> systemic taurine depletion -> cardiomyocyte taurine deficiency -> dilated cardiomyopathy -> cardiac output DOWN [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:slc6a6_activity:positiv.mechanism: SLC6A6 (TauT) is the sodium- and chloride-dependent taurine transporter that maintains systemic taurine homeostasis by intestinal absorption and renal reabsorption. SLC6A6 deficiency depletes plasma and cardiomyocyte taurine to near-undetectable levels, causing dilated cardiomyopathy and reduced cardiac output. do(SLC6A6 LoF) -> systemic taurine depletion -> dilated cardiomyopathy -> cardiac output falls.

causal:influence:sulfite_oxidase_activit.evidence: Isolated sulfite oxidase deficiency OMIM 272300; Wiley JIMD 2024 consensus guidelines (Schwahn et al.): 'elevated levels of plasma and urinary S-sulfocysteine' in SUOX/MoCo deficiency; PMC3509921 (HPLC method for S-sulfocysteine): 'increased 5–50 fold in isolated sulfite oxidase deficiency with no overlap between healthy and affected individuals'; Lehninger (cysteine catabolism, sulfite as intermediate). | intervention: do(SUOX loss-of-function) — isolated sulfite oxidase deficiency OMIM 272300
